principles.title: Isometric training and long-term adaptations
principles.summary: Systematic review reports strength, neuromuscular and hypertrophy adaptations from isometric training; outcomes depend on muscle length, intensity and intent.

principles.title: Isometric vs dynamic resistance training
principles.summary: Meta-analysis supports task specificity: isometric training is particularly effective for isometric strength, while transfer across contraction modes is incomplete.

principles.title: Bench, bar and ring dips
principles.summary: Ring dips showed high upper-limb activation; several muscles were more activated on rings than bench dips and some exceeded bar dips.

principles.title: Ring vs bar muscle-up muscle activity
principles.summary: Ring muscle-up produced greater activation in several upper-limb muscles during pull and push phases compared with bar muscle-up.

principles.title: Push-ups under stable and unstable conditions
principles.summary: Suspension instability altered stabilizer recruitment, including serratus/core-related activation; instability does not uniformly increase every muscle.

principles.title: Static strength elements on rings
principles.summary: Static ring strength elements showed high muscular demand, stabilization requirements and EMG fatigue changes over short holds.

limitations: Movement-specific muscle maps combine direct evidence where available with biomechanics/anatomical inference where direct studies do not exist.
The app never treats muscle coefficients as exact EMG percentages or exact muscle-growth percentages.
Static hold seconds are converted into bounded stimulus-equivalent units for trend tracking; this is an engineering heuristic, not a validated physiological equation.
Muscle-up is modeled as a mixed explosive skill/strength movement; low-rep power work should not be interpreted as equivalent to bodybuilding volume.
